title: U.S. CFTC sets policies on event contract data, using crypto to check financial boxes
summary: The derivatives regulator issues a rule on data reporting for event contracts and new guidance for how crypto assets can be used to meet regulatory requirements.
content: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission has established new policies regarding event contract data reporting. Additionally, the derivatives regulator has issued guidance on how crypto assets can be utilized by firms to meet their financial and regulatory compliance requirements. These measures aim to provide clearer oversight in the evolving digital asset and derivatives markets.

title: Ethereum Foundation doubles protocol security team ahead of overhaul
summary: The foundation said its next upgrade will be harder than the Merge, and the required pace of development will make it easier to ship bugs.
content: The Ethereum Foundation has doubled the size of its protocol security team in preparation for a major network overhaul. The organization stated that its upcoming upgrade will be more complex than the previous Merge event. Officials warned that the faster pace of development required for the transition increases the risk of shipping bugs.

title: CFTC staff say bitcoin, ether can count toward derivatives firms’ operating expenses
summary: Staff at the CFTC issued an advisory saying certain regulated firms may count crypto such as bitcoin and ether toward operating costs.
content: Staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission have issued an advisory stating that certain regulated derivatives firms may count cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ether toward their operating expenses. This guidance provides clarity for companies dealing in digital assets under the regulatory framework, allowing them to include approved virtual currencies as part of the financial resources required to cover day-to-day operational costs.

title: Solana Price Prediction 2030: Is $2,000 SOL Still on the Table After a 75% Crash?
summary: Key takeaways SOL trades near $73, roughly 75% below its January 2025 high of $294, and tracked Binance whale positioning leans bearish (about 20% longs) while around 79% of broader accounts are long. PumpGlass shows a $19.5 million short-liquidation cluster near $79.01 and long-liquidation clusters near $69.39 and $68.01. Solana has lost roughly 75% of its value since reaching an all-time high of $294 in January 2025. Large futures traders are leaning bearish, yet institutional analysts continue to see a future in which SOL trades at four digit prices. So, how realistic is a $2,000 Solana price prediction for 2030? At around $73, SOL is trading at a fraction of the price some of Wall Street’s most optimistic forecasts suggest it could eventually reach. But a steep discount to an analyst’s target does not necessarily make an asset cheap. NewsBTC examined liquidation heatmaps, whale positions, historical price action, network economics and institutional valuation models to understand where Solana stands today and what it could realistically be worth by the end of the decade. The findings paint a more complicated picture than either bulls or bears might expect. Solana Whales Are Betting Against the Crowd Perhaps the most interesting signal right now comes from the derivatives market. According to a November 23 snapshot from PumpGlass, only around 20% of the tracked Binance whale position value was allocated to longs. Meanwhile, approximately 79% of the broader trader accounts were positioned long. Although the two figures measure different aspects of market positioning, the divergence is striking. Large traders appear considerably less optimistic than the wider trading crowd. The average entry price of tracked whale shorts stood near $77.63, compared with $77.05 for whale longs. With SOL trading around $73 at the time of observation, the short side was better positioned. Binance whale and trader positioning for SOL. Source: PumpGlass, November 23, 2026. The on-chain picture offers another reason for caution. On November 19, blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that two large holders had unstaked a combined 2.31 million SOL worth approximately $169.4 million before transferring the tokens to Coinbase Prime-associated addresses. Exchange deposits do not necessarily mean those tokens were sold. Institutional investors use custody platforms for several purposes, including collateral management and portfolio rebalancing. Still, the movement is worth monitoring. What matters now is whether large holders begin accumulating again or whether the recent decline has further to run. Shorts accounted for roughly 72% of those liquidations. SOL had gained around 3.1% over the same rolling period. The recovery is consistent with some bearish positions being forced out of the market. However, a liquidated short is not the same as a new investor buying SOL for the next four years. Until stronger spot demand emerges, traders should be careful about interpreting a short squeeze as the beginning of a sustainable recovery. Liquidation concentrations are modeled estimates, not guaranteed future orders, and can change considerably as traders adjust their positions. Solana Technical Analysis: The Levels That Could Change Everything Solana’s price structure has deteriorated considerably since its September recovery. After closing July near $72.79, SOL climbed to $103 in August and $117.99 in September. The recovery subsequently unraveled, with October closing near $95.35 before prices returned to the low $70s in November. Solana (SOL) price chart, 2026. Source: Binance SOLUSDT, TradingView. Looking at SOL’s historical price action on Binance, using the TradingView SOLUSDT market as the chart reference, five key price regions stand out: SOL price Technical significance $60–$65 Major downside reference $69–$71 Immediate support $75–$80 short term resistance $88–$95 Intermediate recovery zone $100–$118 Broader trend recovery territory The daily Relative Strength Index was in the low 30s in the observed CoinGlass data, suggesting weak momentum and proximity to oversold territory. But oversold markets can remain oversold. A sustained recovery above $80 would be the first encouraging development. Reclaiming $95 and subsequently $100 would provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control. On the downside, failure to hold the $65 range would bring Solana’s 2026 low near $60.42 back into focus. Our technical assessment remains cautious. There is room for a meaningful relief rally, particularly given the nearby short-liquidation exposure, but the broader market structure has yet to establish a convincing reversal. The $73 Token Behind a Multibillion-Dollar Economy While Solana’s price has struggled, its blockchain continues to facilitate substantial financial activity. According to DefiLlama, Solana’s November 23 network metrics included: Network metric Reported value DeFi total value locked $4.68 billion Stablecoin market capitalization $13.14 billion Daily DEX trading volume $1.12 billion Daily active addresses 1.8 million Daily transactions 83.42 million Daily application revenue $2.07 million Daily chain revenue $23,978 There is something particularly interesting about those last two figures. Applications running on Solana generated considerably more revenue than the chain itself under DefiLlama’s respective measurement definitions. This highlights what could become Solana’s biggest valuation challenge. A blockchain can attract substantial activity and billions of dollars in trading volume without its native token capturing a proportional share of that economic value. Cheap transactions are excellent for adoption. Whether they are equally good for SOL’s valuation is another question entirely. That is why Solana’s expansion beyond speculative trading could prove so important. The blockchain’s growing presence in stablecoins, payments and tokenized real-world assets opens the door to financial activity that could persist even when speculative markets cool. Its infrastructure is also evolving. The Solana Foundation reported the activation of Alpenglow in October 2026, targeting transaction finality near 150 milliseconds. November’s introduction of Solana 1.0 marked another milestone in the network’s development. Meanwhile, the announced integration with DTCC’s Tokenization Service, expected in the second half of 2027, could represent a meaningful institutional opportunity. The real test will be how much financial activity these developments ultimately bring onchain, and how much value SOL captures from it. The $1.38 Trillion Problem With a $2,000 Solana Here is something many price predictions overlook: Solana’s token supply will not necessarily remain where it is today. Unlike Bitcoin, SOL has no fixed maximum supply. Its inflationary issuance framework rewards validators and staking participants, while future governance decisions can influence the rate of supply growth. With around 592 million SOL currently circulating, we use an illustrative assumption of 690 million total tokens by 2030 for our valuation scenarios. Outcomes outside these ranges, including substantially greater losses, are possible. Bearish Scenario: $40–$110 Solana remains relevant but struggles to turn network adoption into meaningful economic value for SOL. Institutional projects develop more slowly than expected, competitors gain market share, and speculative trading remains an important source of demand. Solana does not need to fail for this scenario to materialize. It only needs to fall short of the expectations investors have placed on it. Base Scenario: $180–$400 Our central expectation assumes Solana retains its position among the leading smart-contract networks while expanding its role in payments, DeFi and tokenized financial assets. Under this scenario, the network does not need to dominate global finance. It needs to establish a durable position within it and capture more economic value from the applications it supports. Bullish Scenario: $600–$1,000 Solana becomes a major platform for tokenized equities, stablecoin settlements and high-frequency financial applications. Institutional adoption moves beyond announcements, network revenue expands significantly, and the broader cryptocurrency market benefits from favorable liquidity conditions. At $1,000, SOL would trade at approximately 13.8 times its November 23 reference price. Extreme Scenario: $1,500–$2,000+ This is where the most ambitious institutional predictions become conceivable. Solana would need to capture a significant share of a much larger on-chain financial economy, scale its infrastructure accordingly, and translate that activity into sustained demand for SOL. An exceptional cryptocurrency bull market could also temporarily push valuations beyond what underlying economics justify. We would not consider this the most likely outcome based on today’s evidence. The Five Signals That Could Make Us Raise Our Forecast Rather than following every new price target, long-term SOL investors may benefit from monitoring five developments: Stablecoin adoption: Growth in recurring payment and settlement activity beyond speculative trading. Institutional tokenization: Actual financial instruments and trading volumes going live on Solana. Network economics: Sustained growth in fees, economic value and demand for SOL. Institutional capital: Persistent ETF inflows and broader spot-market participation. Technical resilience: Reliable performance under heavy demand without sacrificing security or decentralization. Competition from Ethereum, its scaling ecosystem and specialized financial networks remains a considerable risk. If Solana’s transaction volumes rise while the economic value captured by the network stagnates, we would have reason to lower our valuation assumptions, regardless of how impressive the adoption statistics look. Is Solana Undervalued at $73? The current market offers an interesting contradiction. Solana’s blockchain has established a meaningful financial ecosystem, yet its token is trading roughly 75% below its historical record. Large futures traders are cautious, while institutional research continues to outline substantial long-term opportunities. Our $180 to $400 base-case range for 2030 reflects the possibility that Solana can grow without fulfilling every ambitious expectation placed on it. A move toward $1,000 is conceivable under considerably stronger conditions. At $2,000, however, investors would be betting on Solana becoming one of the world’s most valuable digital financial networks. The opportunity is there. The evidence that would justify such a valuation is not there yet. For now, the most interesting question surrounding Solana is not how many transactions it can process, but how much those transactions will eventually be worth to SOL holders. title: Bitcoin didn’t crash 70%, but Kraken’s order book did – Here’s what went wrong
summary: Kraken's BTC/CAD market's 70% price collapse has raised questions about market-maker liquidity and trading risks.

title: Binance Hack: US Moves to Recover $1.1 Billion, but Who Gets the Money?
summary: Key takeaways US authorities filed a civil forfeiture complaint on November 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the October 29 Binance hack, across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains. Circle froze the funds but says it cannot technically move them, so it proposes issuing replacement USDC to the US after a forfeiture order. Frozen is not recovered: the filings advance the legal-control stage, while final distribution and ownership remain undecided. A separate Abu Dhabi court order adds a second jurisdiction, and Circle’s reserve and supply reporting for the replacement tokens will deserve scrutiny. Nearly four weeks after the Binance hack, US authorities have filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the October theft. The money is already subject to restrictions, but the latest court filings reveal a complication: freezing stolen cryptocurrency is considerably easier than returning it. The complaint, filed on November 23, in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, targets USDC associated with 36 cryptocurrency addresses across 18 blockchains. Federal investigators attribute the October 29 attack to North Korean hacking groups, including the Lazarus Group. The complaint puts the value of the original theft at approximately $6 billion. For Binance, the latest legal action represents another opportunity to recover a portion of its losses. For the wider cryptocurrency industry, however, the case raises questions about the authority stablecoin issuers exercise over digital assets and what happens when governments become involved. Binance Hack Recovery Enters a New Legal Phase The assets targeted by US authorities are not an entirely new discovery. Earlier this month, NewsBTC reported that Circle had frozen approximately $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Binance hack, following cooperation with law enforcement. What has changed is the government’s attempt to establish a legal basis for taking possession of those assets. According to the court documents, US authorities obtained a temporary restraining order on November 12. Prosecutors subsequently requested that the restrictions remain in place throughout the civil forfeiture proceedings. Both Binance and Circle consented to the initial restraining order and the requested extension, according to the government’s November 23 application. The agreement between the companies and federal authorities reduces one immediate obstacle to preserving the funds. It does not, however, resolve the question of their ultimate ownership or distribution. Civil forfeiture proceedings are directed against property believed to be connected to criminal activity. Interested parties can assert legitimate claims to that property through the legal process. In this case, prosecutors are seeking forfeiture of the assets to the United States. That is not the same thing as a court ordering their immediate return to Binance. Circle Cannot Simply Send the Frozen USDC Back Perhaps the most interesting disclosure in the complaint concerns Circle itself. The stablecoin issuer can restrict transfers involving USDC held at particular blockchain addresses. However, that authority does not necessarily give Circle direct control over the wallets holding those tokens. The complaint states that Circle: “ does not have the technical ability to transfer the Defendant Property from the blocklisted Subject Addresses to the United States US forfeiture complaint · November 23 filing Instead, Circle has agreed to issue an equivalent amount of replacement USDC and transfer those tokens to US authorities upon receiving a forfeiture order from the court. The proposed arrangement exposes an unusual feature of centralized stablecoins. An issuer can prevent tokens from circulating without possessing the private keys needed to move them. It also raises an accounting question that deserves attention. If replacement tokens are issued, what ultimately happens to the original frozen USDC, and how will Circle ensure that the treatment of those balances is reflected accurately in its outstanding supply and reserve reporting? The issuance of replacement tokens would not, by itself, prove that USDC had become undercollateralized. Nevertheless, transparency around the implementation would be important for a stablecoin whose credibility depends on confidence in its backing. The immediate concern is not whether Circle can create new tokens. It is whether the entire recovery process can be independently accounted for. The $1.1 Billion Is Not Back With Binance Yet The temptation to describe the Justice Department’s announcement as a billion-dollar recovery is understandable. It is also premature. There are three separate stages involved: restricting access to the stolen assets, obtaining legal authority over them and determining how they will ultimately be distributed. The November 23 filings advance the second stage. They do not establish that the third has been completed. The $1.1 billion Binance recovery process. Source: US District Court for the District of Columbia filings, November 23, 2026. There is also a cross-border complication. On November 18, Reuters reported that an Abu Dhabi court had directed several cryptocurrency companies, including Circle, to preserve digital assets associated with the Binance theft. The involvement of authorities in both the United States and the United Arab Emirates illustrates how a single cryptocurrency theft can generate legal proceedings across multiple jurisdictions. Blockchain transactions may cross national borders without much difficulty. Establishing ownership rights over the assets involved is a considerably less straightforward exercise. That does not mean the US and UAE proceedings are necessarily in conflict. But the ultimate disposition of the funds will require more than an announcement from either government. For investors assessing Binance’s financial position, the distinction between frozen assets and recovered capital is particularly important. Restricted cryptocurrency should not automatically be treated as money already returned to the exchange. The Binance Hack Tests the Case for Centralized Stablecoins For years, the ability of stablecoin issuers to freeze tokens has been criticized by advocates of decentralized finance. The Binance case demonstrates the other side of that argument. Without Circle’s ability to restrict transactions, preserving such a large amount of cryptocurrency for potential recovery would have been more difficult. In this particular case, centralized control has provided a mechanism that may help prevent suspected criminals from benefiting from stolen assets. The uncomfortable question is whether the cryptocurrency industry can benefit from that authority while also demanding meaningful safeguards against its misuse. The answer depends partly on transparency. Token holders should be able to understand why assets were frozen, under what legal authority restrictions remain in place and how disputes over ownership are resolved. The same standard should apply to the exchange, the stablecoin issuer and the government. The next significant development in the Binance case will be the court’s treatment of the forfeiture claim and any competing claims to the assets. Circle’s proposed issuance of replacement USDC will also deserve scrutiny if it proceeds. Until then, the $1.1 billion should be understood as assets subject to an ongoing recovery effort, not a completed repayment. For a cryptocurrency industry that frequently celebrates the speed of moving money, the Binance hack is a reminder that getting it back can be an entirely different business.
content: US authorities have filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking over $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the recent Binance hack. While stablecoin issuer Circle previously froze the funds, it cannot technically move them and proposes issuing replacement tokens upon a final court order. The case highlights cross-border legal complexities and the ongoing debate over centralized control in the cryptocurrency industry.

content_ta: Oxford-ல் நடத்தப்பட்ட ஒரு ஆய்வில், AI agents-கள் குறைபாடுள்ள பணிகளை மதிப்பாய்வு செய்பவர்களை ஏமாற்றி ஒப்புதல் பெற முடியும் என்பது கண்டறியப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த கண்டுபிடிப்பு கல்வி ஒருமைப்பாடு மற்றும் AI-உதவி மதிப்பீடுகளின் நம்பகத்தன்மைக்கு குறிப்பிடத்தக்க ஆபத்துக்களை ஏற்படுத்துகிறது.

title: Bitcoin hands back Monday's Nvidia-driven gains, liquidations triple
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) has dropped 2.2% since midnight UTC to around $59,900, giving back Monday's jump and lagging the stock market's rebound from last week's selloff.
content: Bitcoin dropped 2.2% to around $59,900, erasing the gains it made following Monday's Nvidia-driven market jump. The cryptocurrency's recent price movement has lagged behind the broader stock market's recovery from last week's selloff. Additionally, market liquidations tripled as the leading digital asset experienced this renewed downward pressure, highlighting ongoing volatility in the cryptocurrency sector.
content_ta: திங்கட்கிழமை Nvidia ஏற்படுத்திய சந்தை உயர்வால் கிடைத்த லாபத்தை Bitcoin இழந்தது. இதன் விலை 2.2% சரிந்து சுமார் $59,900 என்ற நிலைக்கு வந்துள்ளது. கடந்த வார சரிவிலிருந்து பங்குச் சந்தை மீண்டு வரும் நிலையில், இந்த கிரிப்டோகரன்சி அதன் வேகத்தைப் பிடிக்கத் தவறிவிட்டது. இதற்கிடையில், இந்த விலை வீழ்ச்சியால் சந்தையில் லிக்விடேஷன்கள் மும்மடங்காக அதிகரித்துள்ளன.

title: Bitcoin’s drop to $55,000 left a record 11.6 million BTC underwater
summary: Bitcoin’s supply in profit fell below its 2022 FTX collapse low, while entities holding 100 to 10,000 BTC continued to accumulate.
content: Bitcoin recently dropped to fifty-five thousand dollars, causing a record eleven point six million BTC to fall underwater. This decline pushed the supply in profit below the low seen during the 2022 FTX collapse. Despite the market downturn, entities holding between one hundred and ten thousand BTC continued to accumulate the cryptocurrency.
content_ta: Bitcoin சமீபத்தில் $55,000 ஆக சரிந்ததால், சாதனை அளவாக 11.6 மில்லியன் BTC நஷ்டத்தில் மூழ்கியது. இதனால் லாபத்தில் உள்ள supply அளவு 2022 FTX வீழ்ச்சியின் போது பதிவான குறைந்த அளவை விடக் கீழுள்ள நிலைக்குத் தள்ளப்பட்டது. சந்தை சரிவை எதிர்கொண்ட போதிலும், 100 முதல் 10,000 BTC வரை வைத்திருக்கும் நிறுவனங்கள் தொடர்ந்து cryptocurrency-ஐ சேகரித்து வருகின்றன.

title: South Korea regulator backs bank-controlled stablecoins after months of dispute
summary: Fintech firms could lead stablecoin ventures, but banks would need to own more than half of any issuer.
content: South Korea's financial regulator has endorsed bank-controlled stablecoins following a lengthy dispute regarding the industry's future structure. Under the updated regulatory approach, fintech firms are permitted to spearhead stablecoin ventures, but traditional banks will be required to maintain majority ownership of over fifty percent in any issuing entity.
content_ta: South Korea-ன் நிதி ஒழுங்குமுறை ஆணையம், stablecoins கட்டமைப்புக் குறித்த மாதக்கணக்கிலான சர்ச்சைக்குப் பிறகு, வங்கி கட்டுப்பாட்டில் உள்ள stablecoins-க்கு ஒப்புதல் அளித்துள்ளது. புதிய விதிகளின்படி, fintech நிறுவனங்கள் stablecoin திட்டங்களை நடத்தலாம், ஆனால் எந்தவொரு issuer நிறுவனத்திலும் பாரம்பரிய banks ஐம்பது சதவீதத்திற்கும் அதிகமான பங்குகளை வைத்திருக்க வேண்டும்.

title: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 as rally on Jensen Huang’s Nvidia return fades
summary: Nasdaq 100 futures fell about 1% after the index surged on Monday, while the Dollar Index held above 104, its highest level since March 2025.
content: Bitcoin fell below $60,000 as a recent market rally driven by Nvidia faded. Meanwhile, Nasdaq 100 futures dropped about 1% following a strong surge earlier in the week, and the Dollar Index remained above 104, marking its highest level in months.
content_ta: Nvidia நிறுவனத்தின் எழுச்சியால் சந்தையில் ஏற்பட்ட உற்சாகம் குறைந்ததால், Bitcoin விலை 60,000 டலருக்கும் கீழே சரிந்தது. இதற்கிடையில், வாரத்தின் தொடக்கத்தில் ஏற்பட்ட உயர்வுக்குப் பிறகு Nasdaq 100 ஃப್ಯೂச்சர்ஸ் சுமார் 1% சரிந்தது. மேலும் Dollar Index 104-க்கு மேல் வர்த்தகமாகி வருகிறது.

title: Bitcoin dips back under $60K as gold seals worst 60-day loss since 1980s
summary: Bitcoin continued to threaten the loss of $60,000 support as gold attempted to bounce from a 60-day losing streak during which it fell nearly 25%.
content: Bitcoin dropped back below the $60,000 threshold as market pressure persisted. title: Cybersecurity Exhibitors at GITEX GLOBAL Put AI Agents at the Top of the Risk Agenda
summary:
Autonomous AI agents are emerging as the next major cybersecurity challenge as they gain access to sensitive data, execute transactions and operate beyond direct human oversight. At GITEX Cyber Valley 2026, taking place at GITEX GLOBAL 2026 from 8–11 December at Dubai Exhibition Centre, Expo City Dubai, cybersecurity leaders will spotlight the growing imperative to govern these autonomous systems as businesses prepare for a new era of AI-driven risks in 2027 and beyond.
 
Headline exhibitor CrowdStrike’s 2026 Global Threat Report underscores the escalating threat landscape, recording an 89 percent increase in attacks by AI-enabled adversaries in 2025. Meanwhile, the World Economic Forum’s Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026 found that 87 percent of respondents identified AI-related vulnerabilities as the fastest-growing cyber risk, highlighting the need for stronger AI governance, identity controls, and enterprise data protection.
 
AI agents could become the internet’s primary users by 2030
 
Cloudflare, a global connectivity cloud company, predicts that AI agents will overtake humans as the internet’s primary users by 2030, transforming how businesses interact and transact online while creating new challenges around identity and authorisation.
 
“The biggest reset in 2027 will be the shift from AI that answers questions to AI agents that take action across the Internet,” said Waseem Hattar, Country Manager, UAE & Oman, Cloudflare. “The teams that win will stop asking ‘is this user real?’ and start asking ‘is this agent authorised?’” 
 
At GITEX GLOBAL, Cloudflare will showcase technologies for building and securing AI agents, including shadow AI visibility, workload protection and a unified gateway for managing AI models. The company is also expanding its UAE data centres to support local control over AI workloads.
 
Millions of AI agents could reshape enterprise security
 
Forcepoint, a cybersecurity specialist in data protection and AI security, warns that autonomous agents will increasingly function as a digital workforce, creating challenges beyond traditional IT oversight.
 
The company predicts that by 2030, a business employing 40,000 people could operate millions of AI-powered working entities, raising questions about who controls them and what information they can access.
 

“As AI tools begin to act on sensitive data, protecting that data and governing the AI become a single discipline,” said Samer Diya, Senior Vice President, EMEA, Forcepoint.
 
Forcepoint will showcase its AI Data Security platform, which protects sensitive information across cloud, networks, endpoints and AI environments while governing autonomous agents and unsanctioned AI activity. Its ARIA AI Assistant enables security teams to create and enforce protection policies using natural language.
 
Zero Trust security extends to autonomous AI identities
 
Keypasco, a cybersecurity and digital identity specialist, believes AI security must evolve beyond protecting models to governing what autonomous agents can do, who authorises their actions and who remains accountable.
 
“By 2030, organisations will manage AI Agents with the same rigour they apply to employees today. Every operational AI Agent will require a verifiable identity, defined authority, delegated permissions, and auditable records,” said Chengi Lin, CEO, Keypasco.
 
At the event, the company will introduce the next evolution of its Trust Identity Platform, extending Zero Trust governance beyond employees and devices to agents that access enterprise systems and execute business workflows.
 
AI agents must meet employee-level security standards
 
Rapid7, a global cybersecurity company specialising in exposure management, threat detection and incident response, identifies greater accountability for AI agents as a major cybersecurity development expected in 2027.
 

“An AI agent with business access needs safeguards comparable to those of a new colleague: an accountable manager, appropriate permissions and defined responsibilities,” said Gopan Sivasankaran, Regional Director – Middle East and Africa, Rapid7. He stressed that significant agent actions must be logged, human approval required where appropriate and access revoked quickly when necessary.
 
Rapid7 will demonstrate its AI-enabled Command Platform at Mindware's stand, using agentic AI workflows to gather evidence, support investigations and automate repetitive security tasks.
 
Global cyber chiefs confront emerging threats
 
The focus on AI governance comes as the UAE Cyber Security Council reports more than 800,000 cyberattack attempts daily. 
 
The Cybersecurity Stage, one of several stages within the wider conference programme, will address sovereign security, nation-state threats, supply-chain vulnerabilities, IT/OT convergence and post-quantum readiness. 
 
Leading the discussions will be H.E. Dr. Mohamed Al Kuwaiti, Head of Cybersecurity, UAE Government; Michelle Bordachar Benoit, National Director, National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCI), Chile; and Ioannis Alexakis, Director General, National Cybersecurity Authority, Greece.
 

“Amid escalating state-sponsored threats and AI-powered attacks, cyber resilience is a strategic imperative. GITEX Cyber Valley convenes the expertise and partnerships essential to advancing the UAE's vision for proactive cyber defence and secure digital progress,” said H.E. Dr. Mohamed Al Kuwaiti.
 
International speakers include Mikko Hyppönen, Chief Research Officer at Sensofusion and a globally recognised cybersecurity researcher; Kevin T. Shin, Head of Information Security, Samsung Semiconductor; Corey Deng, Chief Security Officer, Huawei; and Christian Reilly, Field CTO, Cloudflare.
 
The 46th edition of GITEX GLOBAL, organised by inD under the theme ‘Global Reset 2027’, opens with the GITEX Summit at Dubai World Trade Centre on 7 December, followed by the exhibition at Expo City Dubai alongside Expand North Star, which connects the global startup and investment community. Together, the events will feature more than 6,000 enterprise and startup exhibitors, attracting government leaders, investors and technology buyers worldwide.
 
More information is available at www.gitex.com and www.gitex.com/gitex-cyber-valley

title: GoCardless Completes FCA AI Live Testing as Research Finds 44% of Brits Say AI Providers Should Put Payment Mistakes Right
summary:
GoCardless, a Mollie company, has completed the second cohort of the FCA’s AI Live Testing (AILT) programme and released new research which points to where payer confidence needs to be built for agentic commerce to take off. 
In the survey of 2,184 UK adults, conducted by YouGov on behalf of GoCardless:
36% worry about fraud, hacking or their payment details being stolen if an AI assistant made a payment for them, the most common concern
34% say the area is not regulated well enough yet
32% would not know who would be responsible if something went wrong
30% would not know if they would get their money back
The results point to where confidence needs to be built before consumers let AI assistants pay. 
44% of respondents believe that if an AI assistant makes a payment mistake, such as paying the wrong amount or the wrong business, the company that provides the AI agent should be responsible for putting it right. Meanwhile, 22% believe the payer should be accountable because they granted permission.
 
AI-enabled shopping is already commonplace
 
AI assistants already play a part earlier in the shopping process. In the past three months, 24% of UK adults have used one to research a product and 7% have bought something because it was recommended by an AI assistant. However, only 13% say they are likely to let AI make a payment for them in the next 12 months. Clear demographic splits emerge: the figure increases to 22% for those in London, and 20% for those aged 18-24 compared to just 7% for those over 55. 
 
Payment was the focus of GoCardless’s work in the AILT, the FCA programme in which successful applicants test AI systems in real-world conditions, with regulatory support and oversight. GoCardless developed its agentic checkout through rounds of user testing and feedback from businesses. In September, it took the UK’s first agentic account-to-account payment, collecting a recurring donation for the charity Trussell, and in October it expanded the checkout to one-off agentic payments.
 

Hiroki Takeuchi, co-founder and CEO of GoCardless, said: “Our research indicates that AI is already embedded in how many people shop, but paying is where they pause. Taking part in the AILT let us put a live agentic checkout in front of real payers. That experience will help lay the foundations of agentic commerce across the market. It’s an exciting start but for AI-driven payments to become widely adopted, an open trust framework is essential. It needs the whole ecosystem of industry, regulators and policymakers behind it and we’re proud to play our part.”

title: Form3 Partners With Coinbase Infrastructure to Bring Stablecoin Money Movement to Its Global Customer Base
summary:
Form3, a leading global fintech offering account-to-account payments technology, today announced it is using Coinbase infrastructure to bring stablecoin money movement to its global customer base, offering clients a single hub for money movement. 
Stablecoins are becoming increasingly popular thanks to their ability to enable off-hours cash movement, lower transaction fees, expanded local payments access and faster processing. However, financial institutions moving between fiat and these digital assets face the problem of having to stitch together multiple banking and crypto holding systems, resulting in additional integrations, fragmented processes and the need for manual intervention. This new initiative brings stablecoin payment capabilities into the existing Form3 platform that Tier 1 banks already rely upon.
Form3 customers with a regulated Coinbase account will be able to fund via fiat currency and then mint stablecoins in their Coinbase wallet through Form3’s API.
Form3’s payments platform serves as the financial fabric that enables customers to connect to payment rails across North America, the UK and Europe to deliver seamless instant payments. This new development extends this connectivity to support clients’ adoption of new forms of money, including stablecoins. Form3’s customers include leading Tier 1 banks and fintechs, including J.P. Morgan Payments, Barclays, Santander, and Klarna.
Dave Scola, US CEO at Form3, commented: “Digital assets, like stablecoins, are continuing to gain traction as an effective cross-border payment method. However, unless banks and fintechs have practical ways to integrate stablecoins into their offering, their benefits will be confined to theory only. 
Rather than building a separate asset stack, our focus is on leveraging our existing institutional-grade fiat payments infrastructure which our customers already rely on and collaborating with Coinbase, a market leader in this space, to enable our customers to unlock the value of stablecoins as part of everyday payment operations.”

title: Pliant Secures More Than €200 Million in Additional Financing Capacity to Support European Growth
summary:
Pliant, a global fintech specializing in highly modular B2B payment solutions, today announced that it has secured more than €200 million in additional debt financing capacity through three transactions with Ascory Bank AG and Viola Credit. The financing strengthens Pliant's ability to support growing credit card payment volumes and customer credit card lines across Europe, providing a scalable refinancing foundation for its continued expansion.
The financing structures are designed to address the distinct liquidity requirements of commercial card issuing, including funding customer credit balances and meeting card scheme settlement collaterals. By securing secured financing against both, Pliant can support greater transaction volumes while maintaining a scalable and efficient funding model.
The transactions include two facilities provided by Ascory Bank, a long-standing partner of Pliant. The first uses a securitization structure backed by receivables from Pliant's European corporate credit card business. The second supports collateral requirements associated with Visa's card settlement process (Visa Prefunding Solution), helping Pliant manage the liquidity needed to support increasing card transaction volumes.
The third transaction extends Pliant's existing growth debt facility with Viola Credit, including an option to increase financing capacity. Together, the arrangements provide additional financial flexibility and are expected to support Pliant's anticipated European growth over at least the next two years.
“As our European business continues to scale, it's critical that our financing infrastructure grows alongside it,” said Malte Rau, CEO and co-founder of Pliant. “These agreements give us significantly greater capacity to support our customers' payment needs while continuing to expand our commercial card business. They also reflect the strength of the financial infrastructure we've built and the confidence our financing partners have in Pliant's long-term growth.”
“We have worked with Pliant for more than six years, so it is particularly rewarding to see how our partnership has developed over time,” said Lukas Diehl, Head of Corporate Clients at Ascory Bank. “During that period, both Pliant and Ascory have grown significantly, while maintaining the trust and close collaboration that have characterized our relationship from the beginning. With this financing, we are taking the next step and providing Pliant with a flexible solution that supports its continued growth.”
“We’re excited to continue backing Pliant as the company expands into new markets while maintaining a strong European presence,” Elad Friedman, Managing Director at Viola Credit. “Over the past years Pliant has emerged as the leading Europe HQed provider of corporate credit card solutions, and together with the new capital raise will continue its growth into new verticals and markets.”
The announcement follows Pliant's recently announced $80 million Series C funding round, which will support further international expansion and development of its AI-powered payment infrastructure. The new debt financing arrangements complement that investment by providing additional capacity to support Pliant's growing European commercial card business.

title: Zopa Bank Joins Warm Homes Loan Scheme to Help Millions of Brits Cut the Cost of Green Home Upgrades
summary:
Zopa, the British digital bank pioneer with 2 million customers, has joined the government’s Warm Homes Loan Scheme to help eligible customers lower the cost of their green home upgrades. 
Zopa is offering eligible customers lower-cost financing on heat pumps, solar panels, and solar battery storage at rates ranging from 3.6% to 4.6% APR over 3 to 10 years, available through participating installation partners. 
For example, a customer borrowing £10,000 over 10 years at 4.6% APR would pay £25.61 less each month than on an equivalent loan at 9.9% APR, cutting total interest costs by 55.7% and saving the customer approximately £3,073 across the full term.*
Applications for Zopa finance are subject to eligibility, credit and affordability checks.
The announcement comes as more households and businesses invest in technology to generate and store energy than ever before. There were around 36,000 certified battery storage installations across the UK in the first half of 2026 alone, almost double the number recorded in the same period a year earlier.
Making these technologies more affordable will be key to sustaining that momentum. For many customers, however, the upfront cost remains a barrier to making these improvements. 
Tim Waterman, Chief Commercial Officer at Zopa Bank, said: “Everyone should have the opportunity to live in a home that’s warmer, greener and more affordable to run. But for too many households, the upfront cost of technologies like heat pumps and solar panels stands in the way of that transition.
“By joining the Warm Homes Loan Scheme, Zopa is helping to turn the ambition for a warmer, more affordable home into reality. By bringing down the cost of finance and giving eligible customers the option to spread payments over up to 120 monthly instalments, we’re enabling more people to take greater control of their energy use, offering more choice over how they pay alongside reassurance of a fully regulated experience.”
Minister for Local Jobs and Energy Minister McCluskey said: “Zopa Bank joining the Warm Homes Loan Scheme is great news for consumers, as we have seen significant demand since we launched last month.
“Low and no interest loans allow people to benefit from clean energy tech such as solar, heat pumps and batteries - with no upfront costs - so more families can save on their bills.”
The news further supports Zopa’s entry into green lending and Zopa for Business' provision of more payment and finance tools for UK businesses.
In 2024, Zopa partnered with Octopus Energy to enter the £23bn renewable energy market; in 2026, it has partnered with Hive Energy and Segen to give customers more financing options when upgrading their homes.
This year’s partnerships launched alongside Zopa for Business, Zopa’s bolstered business offering that brings payments, retail finance, auto finance and embedded partnerships into a single platform.
Designed to help businesses accept payments, offer finance and complete more sales by integrating once without juggling multiple providers, it follows Zopa’s acquisition of payments platform Rvvup in 2025 and point-of-sale finance platform DivideBuy in 2023.
These developments contribute to Zopa’s sustained profitable growth, having originated £1.6 billion in new lending in the first half of 2026, up 35% year on year. As a result, Zopa is now the UK’s largest open-market lender for personal loans by volume and among the top three by value. 
One of the UK’s highest rated and most celebrated financial brands, Zopa has been recognised with over 10 British Bank Awards, holds a Trustpilot rating of 4.6/5, and has one of the highest customer satisfaction scores in the industry.

title: Cytora and GBG Partner to Bring Identity and Financial Crime Checks Into Commercial Underwriting
summary:
Cytora, the risk digitization and automation platform for commercial insurance, and GBG, the AI trust intelligence platform, today announced a partnership that puts identity verification, business verification and financial crime screening inside Cytora's risk workflows. 
Every commercial submission raises two questions before anything else can happen: who is this, and can we do business with them? Today those answers usually arrive late, assembled by hand from company registries, sanctions lists and internal checks, often after an underwriter has already formed a view. Under this partnership, they arrive with the submission.
As each risk is digitized, the Cytora platform queries GBG to resolve the insured entity and return:
Identity verification (KYC): confirms the individuals behind the business are real and correctly identified
Business verification (KYB): confirms the entity exists, and shows its structure and [ultimate ownership, where available by jurisdiction]
Sanctions, PEP and AML screening: checks against global watchlists, with the evidence attached to the record
The result is a decision-ready risk that can be evaluated against the insurer's own appetite rules. Clean risks flow through to straight-through processing. Anything that warrants a closer look is routed to specialist review with the supporting evidence already gathered, so the reviewer starts from a position of knowing rather than asking. Because the checks run inside the workflow, every one of them is logged and auditable.
For insurers writing financial lines, commercial package, specialty and other complex risks, this turns due diligence from a task performed after submission into a control that operates during it, without adding a step for the underwriter.
GBG joins Cytora's Data Partner Ecosystem as its identity and financial crime intelligence partner. 
The partnership adds a capability that has been largely absent from the commercial insurance data landscape. Cytora's ecosystem already spans property, climate, cyber, financial and geospatial data; identity and financial crime intelligence completes the picture at the point where every risk relationship begins.
Zurich scaled Cytora's agentic AI to five countries in 90 days and is scaling AI-powered risk digitization across 20+ markets within the first 16 months, reducing manual processing time by over 80 per cent. GBG supports more than 20,000 customers worldwide and processes around 800 million identity checks a year.
“Every risk decision starts with knowing who you are dealing with. With GBG in our Data Partner Ecosystem, insurers can verify the entity and screen for financial crime as the submission is digitized, so underwriters start from a verified risk, not a question.”
Juan De Castro, COO, Cytora
“Financial crime checks shouldn't be the step that slows an underwriter down, or the one that gets skipped when the queue is long. Inside Cytora, they run as each submission arrives. Clean risks move. The ones that deserve a closer look get one, with the evidence already attached.”
Gus Tomlinson, Chief Product & Technology Officer, GBG

title: BlackRock opens tokenized money market fund with $100 million in assets to Hong Kong investors
summary: Key takeaways BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, for investors in Hong Kong. The tokenized D OnChain class lists a minimum investment of HK$10, against HK$10 million for the conventional I class, but access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors. The fund gives HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Anchorpoint Financial, a use beyond payments, while the returns still come from the underlying short-term instruments. Tokenization does not remove dealing deadlines or redemption limits, and the disclosures reviewed did not yet give total fund assets or current yields. BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, giving investors in Hong Kong a new way to move money between traditional investments and blockchain-based financial products. The BlackRock tokenized fund, known formally as the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, supports both conventional and tokenized investment units. It also introduces a use case for HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint Financial. The development follows Anchorpoint’s plans to expand HKDAP to Solana, announced in late October. However, there is an interesting detail in BlackRock’s product disclosures. One of the fund’s tokenized classes requires a minimum investment of just HK$10, while access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors. The technology may be making financial products more accessible, but the institutions behind them still decide who gets through the door. What BlackRock’s New Tokenized Fund Actually Offers BlackRock announced regulatory authorization for the fund on September 10, with its product listings identifying November 16 as the inception date. The commercial launch was reported on Tuesday, November 24. Unlike many of the investment products available across decentralized finance, BlackRock’s fund does not depend on cryptocurrency lending, liquidity pools or token incentives to generate returns. Its investment strategy revolves around short-term financial instruments, including government-backed securities and bank deposits. Investors gain exposure to those assets through fund units. With tokenized units, blockchain technology is used to maintain ownership records. BlackRock’s official product disclosure lists a minimum initial investment of HK$10 for its D OnChain class, alongside a management fee of 0.31% and daily income distributions. BlackRock product disclosure for the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund. Source: BlackRock. For comparison, the fund’s conventional I class requires a minimum initial investment of HK$10 million. The difference is substantial, although a lower investment minimum should not be confused with unrestricted access. Different share classes and distribution channels come with their own conditions. A Stablecoin That Can Finally Do More Than Move Money Perhaps the most interesting part of BlackRock’s launch is what it means for HKDAP. Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture between Standard Chartered, Animoca Brands and HKT, received its stablecoin issuer licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in April. Until now, much of the discussion surrounding regulated Hong Kong dollar stablecoins has focused on payments, transfers and their potential role in financial infrastructure. BlackRock’s fund introduces another practical application. Eligible investors can use digital money denominated in Hong Kong dollars to access investments denominated in the same currency. In its September announcement, BlackRock stated: “ “Investors will be able to use HKDAP” to subscribe to and redeem investments from the fund. BlackRock · September announcement Imagine a company that already holds HKDAP for operational payments. Instead of leaving all its surplus liquidity in stablecoins, it could potentially move some of that balance into a money market fund and earn investment income while the money is not needed. The important distinction is that the stablecoin itself is not generating the fund’s returns. The underlying financial instruments are. Conceptual illustration based on BlackRock’s stated fund structure and digital-cash subscription arrangements. Not a technical settlement architecture or guarantee of immediate redemption. For stablecoin issuers, this kind of integration could ultimately prove more valuable than simply securing another exchange listing. It gives businesses a reason to hold and use digital cash beyond cryptocurrency trading. The Blockchain Is Always Open. The Fund Isn’t. There is still a noticeable difference between what blockchain infrastructure can do and what BlackRock’s product currently offers. The D OnChain class lists a daily dealing schedule with an 11 AM Hong Kong time trading deadline and settlement on the trade date. Anyone familiar with decentralized finance will recognize the contrast. A blockchain does not stop processing transactions because a bank has closed or a fund has passed its dealing deadline. But tokenizing an investment does not automatically change the operating hours, liquidity arrangements or legal obligations of the underlying fund. BlackRock also warns that technology failures, compromised wallets and disruptions involving blockchain service providers could interfere with investors’ ability to access or redeem their holdings. Restrictions on redemptions are possible under stressed market conditions, while investors remain exposed to potential capital losses. These limitations are not necessarily a failure of tokenization. Institutional investors have regulatory, custody and accounting obligations that cannot simply be removed by deploying a smart contract. Still, if investors ultimately have to work around many of the same deadlines and intermediaries they encounter in traditional finance, the immediate advantages of tokenization become narrower. Hong Kong Is Building The Infrastructure Around Tokenized Finance Earlier this month, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority expanded its EnsembleTX settlement initiative to support continuous settlement using tokenized central bank money. The initiative involves several major financial institutions, including BlackRock, and supports applications involving tokenized deposits and investment funds. These developments are gradually connecting different parts of the financial system that previously operated separately. There are now regulated digital currencies, tokenized investment products and settlement infrastructure being developed to move value between them. However, BlackRock’s latest launch also shows why the size of the tokenization market should not be measured solely by the number of financial products being brought onto blockchains. The more interesting figures will be how much money actually enters these funds through digital cash, how frequently investors move between the two products and whether those transactions become cheaper or faster. BlackRock’s product disclosures reviewed for this article did not yet provide usable figures for total fund assets or current yields. Nor does the launch establish unrestricted access through decentralized exchanges or lending protocols. Those are the developments worth watching before declaring that tokenized finance has moved beyond institutional adoption and into the hands of ordinary crypto users. Hong Kong now has another piece of the infrastructure. The next challenge is getting people to use it.

title: Beyond the Model: Why Data Is Still the Hardest Problem in Enterprise AI
summary:
As frontier models become more widely available, OceanBase is betting on a unified “lakebase” platform and an open-source AI database to win over banks and global enterprises.
 
At fintech conferences over the past two years, one question has dominated conversations about AI: which model is smartest, fastest, or cheapest to use? Banks, insurers, and payment firms have invested heavily in testing frontier models, hoping the right choice might give them a lasting edge.
 
OceanBase CEO Evan Yang believes the bigger challenge lies elsewhere: in the data behind the models.
 
Speaking at OceanBase’s AI Data Conference in Beijing on November 24, 2026, he argued that natural-language tools can make software development look deceptively easy, but the hard work has not disappeared. It has shifted.
 
Drawing on Fred Brooks’s 1986 essay No Silver Bullet, Yang distinguished between “accidental” complexity—the friction better tools can reduce—and “essential” complexity, which remains. In enterprise AI, he said, much of that complexity sits in the data.
 

“The more capable our models become, the more unforgiving our data problems look,” he said. “Solving that essential complexity is the work that will decide who actually captures value from this technology.”
 
Intelligence is becoming more accessible. Proprietary data still matters.
 
As model capabilities spread and prices fall, access to raw intelligence alone may offer less lasting differentiation. For banks and insurers, a more distinctive asset is the data they already hold: transaction histories, risk decisions, operational records, and other information tied to their businesses.
 
In his keynote, Yang highlighted three areas where companies can do more with that data:
 


Private data: Public information is only part of the picture. A company’s own records can provide context that general-purpose models do not have.
Multimodal data: Rows and columns capture only part of reality. Text, images, audio, and sensor feeds can also matter, such as when an insurer assesses an accident or a lender evaluates non-standard collateral.
Well-governed data: Large data volumes are of limited use if they are not indexed, governed, and connected to clear business meaning.
 
OceanLake brings data and AI workloads together
 
To address those gaps, Yang outlined four principles for AI-era data infrastructure: a converged lakebase, multimodal data fusion, governance designed for agents, and openness.
 
At the conference, OceanBase introduced OceanLake, an integrated lakebase AI data platform built around those principles. Unveiled alongside the conference announcement, OceanLake brings transactional, analytical, and AI workloads together on a single copy of data, reducing the need to move information between separate databases, warehouses, and AI stores. The platform also includes a business semantic layer and an agent runtime intended to give AI agents shared context and guardrails.
 
This architectural convergence is notable: Databricks—named a Leader in Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems for five consecutive years as of 2025—has made a similar bet with its own Lakebase and LTAP architecture, validating that the durable competitive layer in enterprise AI is the data infrastructure beneath the models.
 
OceanBase cited an early deployment at Ping An Life Insurance, where typical data query delivery times were reportedly reduced from two to five days to about 15 minutes.
 
OceanBase also announced that it is open-sourcing OceanSeek, its agent-focused AI database, under the Apache 2.0 licence. According to the announcement, OceanSeek combines real-time read and write capabilities with analytics, open lake storage, and hybrid search, offering developers an open foundation for agent workloads.
 
Financial-sector credentials and international growth

title: Microsoft’s ‘Code Red’ Exposes Crypto’s Own Cloud Problem
summary: Key takeaways Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” to overhaul its engineering and crisis response after a global outage on November 12-13 that lasted about 24 hours. Coinbase’s May outage was traced to a cooling failure in an AWS data center: all five matching engine nodes were in the same building, and three went offline, disrupting trading, deposits and withdrawals for about eight hours. Moving assets off exchanges does not remove the reliance on centralized infrastructure, because wallets often depend on third-party RPC providers rather than the user’s own node. The issue is not that crypto firms use the cloud but whether they have credible alternatives when it fails, as more assets move onto blockchains. Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” initiative to overhaul its engineering and crisis response following a global service outage that lasted approximately 24 hours. For an industry built around the idea of decentralization, crypto has good reason to pay attention. According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, the technology giant is reconsidering how it prevents and responds to major infrastructure failures after its November 12-13 outage disrupted businesses, government operations and financial firms. Crypto likes to position itself as an alternative to centralized infrastructure. Yet some of its largest businesses depend on the same handful of cloud computing companies, and the consequences of that reliance have already been felt by traders. How A Cooling Failure Brought Coinbase Trading To A Halt In May, Coinbase experienced an infrastructure failure that demonstrated how surprisingly fragile access to cryptocurrency markets can be. The exchange’s official incident report, published on June 1, traced the disruption to a cooling equipment failure inside an Amazon Web Services (AWS) data center. Coinbase had five matching engine nodes located within the same building. Three went offline during the incident, leaving the system without enough functioning nodes to operate normally. The exchange had not implemented an automated mechanism to switch its matching engine to another availability zone. A separate failure involving AWS’s managed event-streaming infrastructure complicated the recovery further. For approximately eight hours, customers experienced severe disruptions affecting trading, deposits and withdrawals. Restoring the remaining systems took roughly another 12 hours. “ “The duration of the outage is unacceptable to us,” Coinbase acknowledged in its subsequent investigation. Coinbase · June 1 incident report This was not the first time the exchange had encountered such problems. An AWS outage in October 2025 resulted in three hours and 17 minutes of degraded performance for Coinbase customers. Despite these incidents, the relationship between cryptocurrency businesses and cloud providers continues to deepen. More recently, Coinbase and AWS partnered to bring x402 payments to CloudFront publishers, bringing blockchain-based payments into existing web infrastructure. The uncomfortable part is that the blockchains themselves did not need to fail for customers to lose access to exchange services. A decentralized settlement network is of limited immediate use to someone whose assets are sitting inside an exchange they cannot access. Your Crypto Wallet May Be Less Decentralized Than You Think Moving assets away from centralized exchanges does reduce some of these risks. However, it does not necessarily eliminate reliance on centralized infrastructure. Consider an Ethereum wallet. When a user opens the application to check their balance or send a transaction, the wallet generally communicates with an Ethereum node through a remote procedure call, commonly known as an RPC. That connection allows the application to retrieve blockchain information and submit signed transactions. How a wallet app connects to Ethereum through an RPC connection. Many users rely on infrastructure operated by third-party providers rather than running their own nodes. If the provider becomes unavailable, the wallet may struggle to display balances or broadcast transactions, even while Ethereum continues producing blocks. In an RPC service outage, the assets can remain intact on the blockchain even when the wallet’s usual connection to the network stops working. Ethereum’s own node documentation acknowledges that widespread reliance on cloud hosting could introduce a common point of failure. Distribution of Ethereum nodes. The distribution of Ethereum nodes also raises questions about infrastructure concentration. Having thousands of independently operated nodes does not necessarily eliminate shared dependencies if many rely on the same hosting providers. Hosting of Ethereum nodes across providers. Shared infrastructure can create security risks as well as availability problems. NewsBTC previously covered the debate over verifier and RPC security following the KelpDAO exploit. That incident was an exploit, not a routine cloud outage. There are alternatives. Users can connect compatible wallets to another RPC provider or operate their own Ethereum nodes. Developers can also design applications to switch between independently operated infrastructure providers when one becomes unavailable. But these options are not always obvious to the average person opening a wallet on their phone. The industry has spent years making crypto easier to use, often by hiding much of its technical complexity. In doing so, it has sometimes reintroduced the dependencies that blockchain technology was intended to reduce. Centralization Is Sometimes A Deliberate Engineering Choice It would be easy to criticize every cryptocurrency company that uses Amazon, Google or Microsoft infrastructure. The reality is more complicated. Coinbase explained that keeping its matching engine nodes physically close together was a deliberate decision intended to meet the speed and capacity requirements of its markets. Separating those systems introduces communication delays. Running redundant infrastructure also costs money, particularly when companies must synchronize large amounts of financial information across multiple locations. Cloud computing providers offer considerable engineering resources and operational capabilities that smaller crypto companies would struggle to reproduce independently. The problem is not simply that crypto businesses use centralized services. It is whether they have credible alternatives when those services fail. Coinbase subsequently outlined plans to improve recovery across availability zones and conduct regular failover exercises in production environments. Those are useful commitments, although publishing a recovery plan and successfully executing one during an unexpected outage are two different things. What Microsoft’s Code Red Means For Crypto There is no established evidence that Microsoft’s latest initiative was prompted by a failure of cryptocurrency networks. The relevance lies elsewhere. As financial institutions bring more assets onto blockchains, the reliability of the infrastructure connecting investors to those networks becomes increasingly important. A tokenized investment fund may exist on a distributed ledger, but investors can still depend on centralized custody providers, banking services, identity verification systems and applications to manage their holdings. A decentralized exchange may execute trades through smart contracts, but its website and the infrastructure connecting users to those contracts can introduce separate vulnerabilities. Crypto companies should be demonstrating how their products behave when their preferred infrastructure provider goes offline. Can users still submit transactions? Can traders cancel orders? Can another operator take over without waiting for an engineering team to intervene? Microsoft’s reported response to its November outage is a reminder that even companies with enormous technical resources can discover weaknesses in systems they previously considered reliable. Crypto does not need to abandon cloud computing. It needs to stop treating decentralization at the blockchain level as proof that everything built around it is equally resilient.

The incident highlights crypto's heavy reliance on centralized cloud infrastructure. Coinbase previously suffered a major trading outage traced to an AWS data center cooling failure, while many Ethereum wallets depend on third-party RPC providers rather than independent nodes, exposing shared vulnerabilities across the industry.

summary: The moves may cement Mark Wiedman as a potential successor to CEO Bill Demchak and lend continuity to a bank that, while growing, has seen changes in two high-profile C-suite slots in 18 months.

title: FM Summit London 2026 Brings Financial Services Leaders Together for a Day of Insights, Connections and Industry-Shaping Discussions
summary:
FM Summit London 2026 brought together the financial services industry at Old Billingsgate, London, for its 15th edition, creating a meeting point for senior decision-makers, industry leaders, financial institutions, brokers and technology providers.
With a programme focused on the developments transforming financial services, the summit combined high-level discussions, expert perspectives and valuable face-to-face connections.
Throughout the summit day, the venue was filled with conversations, networking and business meetings, reflecting the continued importance of uniting the financial services community for direct, in-person connection.
The summit experience began ahead of the main event, with the Opening Networking Blitz at The Folly on 23 November, giving attendees an opportunity to reconnect with familiar faces and make new introductions before the main summit.
Conversations that matter: From financial services to digital assets
The conference programme provided a platform for some of the industry's most thought-provoking conversations, bringing different perspectives to the stage and encouraging attendees to look beyond current market developments.
The summit opened with a conversation on AI, “AI & Trading 2027: From Copilots to Colleagues”, an intriguing panel discussion featuring Steven J. Hatzakis, Global Director of Research at ForexBrokers.com, Yangling Li, Head Quant at BestX, Andrew Ralich, CEO & Co-Founder at oneZero, Jon Light, Senior Director of Product at Devexperts, Hugh Whelan, President of ACI UK, Financial Markets Association, and Christoforos Theodoulou, Chief Business Officer at MetaQuotes. The panelists took a deep dive into the applicability of AI in trading, data quality, models, controls, and beyond.
Later in the day, Lord Peter Cruddas took a trip down memory lane when he founded CMC Markets, offering valuable insights into leadership and the brokerage firm’s longevity as CMC Markets turned 40. His perspective was captured in the CMC anniversary discussion titled “CMC at 35: Lord Peter Cruddas in Conversation,” a statement of brokerage leadership from tradition to the AI era.
Next, “Part of The Landscape? Digital Assets & TradFi Liquidity” brought to the stage Ian Daniels, COO & Global Head at eFX, Chris Knight, Managing Director at LMAX Digital, Waqar Chodri, Managing Director, Global Head, Digital Assets at Standard Chartered Bank, Katryna Hanush, Managing Director, Business Development & Partnerships at Wintermute, and David Brickell, Head of Distribution at FRNT Financial, to examine the evolving relationship between traditional finance and digital assets. The discussion addressed the changing liquidity landscape and the implications for institutional markets and financial infrastructure.
The programme also welcomed Lord Kulveer Ranger for “From Westminster to the Boardroom: In Conversation With Lord Kulveer Ranger.” In conversation with Duska Nedeljkovic, Head of Conferences at Ultimate Group, Lord Ranger brought a perspective shaped by his experience in Westminster and business leadership, exploring the relationship between public policy, government and commercial decision-making.
These discussions reflected the summit's commitment to bringing relevant voices and perspectives together, addressing not only where the industry stands today but also the opportunities and challenges ahead.
Bringing the industry together
Beyond the conference stages, the exhibition floor provided opportunities for companies to showcase their solutions, strengthen existing relationships and establish new business connections.
Leading companies, including LMAX Group, Plus500, oneZero, PLUGIT, Adaptive, Edge Hound, AEGIS Trading Technology, MetaQuotes, Devexperts, Acuity and CXM Prime, were among the participating brands.
Business Connect Roundtables and One-to-One meetings further supported meaningful conversations in a different format and enabled connections between professionals around shared business interests and industry priorities.
15 editions of bringing the industry together
Returning to Old Billingsgate for its 15th edition gave FM Summit London 2026 particular significance. The venue, closely associated with the event's legacy, provided the setting for another chapter in its ongoing journey of connecting the global financial services community.
The success of this edition reflects the importance of creating spaces where industry professionals can exchange ideas, build relationships and explore new opportunities.
FM Summits would like to thank all attendees, speakers, sponsors, exhibitors, partners and supporting media for being part of FM Summit London 2026 and contributing to another memorable edition.
As the industry continues to evolve, the conversations started in London will continue well beyond the summit itself.
One Day. One Venue. One Industry.
